# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.

textkit/__init__.py
textkit/slug.py

1| import re

   3| def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   4|     """Turn arbitrary text into a URL slug: lowercase, ASCII letters and
   5|     digits, words separated by single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphens."""
   6|     text = text.lower()
   7|     text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)

The bug is clear: after replacing non-alphanumeric characters with hyphens, consecutive hyphens aren't collapsed and leading/trailing hyphens aren't stripped.

content:
Both tests pass and the issue's examples now produce the expected output. The fix was minimal:

1. Changed the regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` so runs of non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single hyphen (fixes `hello--world-` → `hello-world`).
2. Added `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens (fixes `--a--b--` → `a-b`).

The public signature is unchanged.

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify in textkit/slug.py by changing the replacement regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` (collapsing consecutive non-alphanumeric characters into a single hyphen) and adding `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. This makes `slugify("Hello,  World!")` return `"hello-world"` and `slugify("--a--b--")` return `"a-b"`; the public signature is unchanged and the test suite passes.
